producer_report.summary: Checks in athena.toml now take an optional `paths` filter. A check whose filter matches no changed path is recorded as passed with the note "not run: no changed path can affect it". A check with no filter, or any check when the change list is empty, always runs. The shipped fmt, clippy and test checks of both `change` and `study` carry the filter, so a docs-only change skips all three. Patterns: `dir/` is a prefix, `*.ext` a suffix, anything else a whole path or file name. The matching code is `path_matches` and `check_applies` in athena-data config.rs. `CheckSpec::applies_to` in capability.rs calls it, and the run loop in run.rs uses that. Both capabilities pass `paths` through. I added decision D79, a CHANGELOG entry and a README line. The final fmt, clippy and test runs were all clean.

checks_run.note: Every suite reported ok, no failures.

open_issues: The filter list must be maintained by hand. A file that only a build script or test reads at runtime, outside the listed paths, would not trigger the checks.
defaults.toml and run_pin_tests.rs are listed as deliverables but needed no edits, so I left them unchanged.
The run-loop skip itself has no direct test. The tests cover the matching logic and the shipped filters, and the existing lifecycle tests still pass.
mistakes: I forgot `paths: None` in the CheckSpec literals in checks.rs, then fixed it. The first full test run printed too much output, so I re-ran with -q.
learnings: The cli tests' common/mod.rs builds its own check table, so it is unaffected by `paths`.
Tests embed athena.toml and defaults.toml with include_str!, so both are in the filter.
